# SessionTranscript golden vectors

SYNTHETIC, generated by TestGenerateSessionTranscriptGoldens from the
OID4VPHandover / OID4VPDCAPIHandover constructors (sessiontranscript.go) with
the fixed inputs in sessiontranscript_test.go (tClientID, tNonce, tThumbprint,
tRespURI, tOrigin). They guard against unintended byte-level drift; they are
NOT an independent check of the encoding, because they are produced by the code
they test.

The independent check lives in the same test file as
`TestSessionTranscript_SpecVectors`: the worked examples published in
[OpenID4VP 1.0 Annex B.2.6.1 and B.2.6.2] — input JWK, HandoverInfo, Handover
and SessionTranscript in hex — reproduced byte-for-byte. Those expected bytes
come from the specification, so they cannot agree with a wrong implementation.

Encoding:

    SessionTranscript           = [null, null, Handover]
    OID4VPHandover              = ["OpenID4VPHandover", SHA-256(CBOR(OpenID4VPHandoverInfo))]
    OpenID4VPHandoverInfo       = [clientId, nonce, jwkThumbprint, responseUri]
    OID4VPDCAPIHandover         = ["OpenID4VPDCAPIHandover", SHA-256(CBOR(OpenID4VPDCAPIHandoverInfo))]
    OpenID4VPDCAPIHandoverInfo  = [origin, nonce, jwkThumbprint]

    clientId      = tstr   ; includes the Client Identifier Prefix
    nonce         = tstr
    jwkThumbprint = bstr   ; RFC 7638 SHA-256 thumbprint of the reader's ephemeral
                           ; response-encryption key, as RAW DIGEST BYTES; CBOR
                           ; null when the response is not encrypted
    responseUri   = tstr   ; response_uri or redirect_uri, per response mode
    origin        = tstr   ; no "origin:" prefix

`jwkThumbprint` was previously emitted as the printable base64url text string.
That produces a different transcript from the one every conformant wallet signs,
so mdoc device authentication failed for all encrypted responses. Corrected
against the primary specification text and its published vectors; the
constructors now take the thumbprint as `[]byte`, which makes the text form
unrepresentable at the API boundary. `TestOID4VPHandover_RejectsTextThumbprintEncoding`
pins the historical bytes so the regression cannot return unnoticed.
